letters.alef: Alef. Soft glottal stop or silent. Picture of an ox.
letters.bet: Bet. Sound: B. Picture of a house.
letters.gimel: Gimel. Sound: G. Picture of a camel.
letters.dalet: Dalet. Sound: D. Picture of a door.
letters.he: He. Sound: H. Picture of a window.
letters.vav: Vav. Sound: V. Picture of a hook.
letters.zayin: Zayin. Sound: Z. Picture of a weapon.
letters.chet: Chet. Soft throat sound, like ch in Bach. Picture of a fence.
letters.tet: Tet. Sound: T. Picture of a basket.
letters.yod: Yod. Sound: Y. Picture of a hand.
letters.kaf: Kaf. Sound: K. Picture of a palm.
letters.lamed: Lamed. Sound: L. Picture of a goad.
letters.mem: Mem. Sound: M. Picture of water.
letters.nun: Nun. Sound: N. Picture of a fish.
letters.samekh: Samekh. Sound: S. Picture of a support.
letters.ayin: Ayin. Deep throat sound, often silent in English reading. Picture of an eye.
letters.pe: Pe. Sound: P. Picture of a mouth.
letters.tsade: Tsade. Sound: TS. Picture of a hook.
letters.qof: Qof. Sound: Q. Picture of the horizon.
letters.resh: Resh. Sound: R. Picture of a head.
letters.shin: Shin. Sound: SH. Picture of a tooth.
letters.tav: Tav. Sound: T. Picture of a mark.
letters.kaf-sofit: Kaf sofit. Final form of Kaf. Sound: K. Counts five hundred in mispar.
letters.mem-sofit: Mem sofit. Final form of Mem. Sound: M. Counts six hundred in mispar.
letters.nun-sofit: Nun sofit. Final form of Nun. Sound: N. Counts seven hundred in mispar.
letters.pe-sofit: Pe sofit. Final form of Pe. Sound: P. Counts eight hundred in mispar.
letters.tsade-sofit: Tsade sofit. Final form of Tsade. Sound: TS. Counts nine hundred in mispar.

names.abraham: Abraham. Meaning: father of a great multitude.
names.moses: Moses. Meaning: taken out, drawn forth.
names.israel: Israel. Meaning: who prevails with God.
names.mary: Mary. Meaning: bitterness, rebellion; also exalted.
names.peter: Peter. Meaning: a rock or stone.

guides.temple: Welcome to the temple walk. Body is the outer court, soul the inner court, and spirit the holy of holies. Glory is the center. Open a gate, read its verse, and mark it walked when you are ready. This is a quiet walk beside Scripture — not a ritual.
